questions.question: When stopping to pick up students, a bus driver should:

options.text: Put the vehicle in park.
Put the vehicle in first gear.
Put the vehicle in reverse.
Put the vehicle in third gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put the vehicle in park.
questions.explanation: When stopping to pick up students, put the school bus in park. If the transmission has no park setting, put the vehicle in neutral instead.

questions.question: Loading a school bus:

options.text: Is not dangerous.
Does not need supervision.
Should be done quickly.
Can be dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be dangerous.
questions.explanation: More students are killed during loading and unloading of school buses than while riding in them. School bus drivers must follow safety procedures during loading and unloading.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, you must check all of the following, except:

options.text: That the oil pressure gauge works.
That the oil pressure warning light turns off, or that the gauge shows normal oil pressure.
That the oil temperature gauge rises to normal operating temperature, if equipped.
That the oil pressure gauge comes on when brakes are used.

questions.correctAnswerText: That the oil pressure gauge comes on when brakes are used.
questions.explanation: Check that the oil pressure gauge works. The gauge should show normal oil pressure, or the warning light should turn off. If equipped with an oil temperature gauge, it should gradually rise to normal operating temperature.

questions.question: What happens if a driver exceeds the allowed number of looks during an exercise?

options.text: They must start the exercise again.
They automatically fail the basic vehicle control skills test.
They fail only that exercise.
Three points are deducted from their test score.

questions.correctAnswerText: They automatically fail the basic vehicle control skills test.
questions.explanation: During the basic vehicle control skills test, a driver can exit their vehicle to check position. This is called a "look." Using more than two looks in any exercise (except straight line backing) causes automatic failure. Using more than one look during straight line backing also causes automatic failure.

questions.question: When backing into an alley, you should first:

options.text: Pull directly into the alley parking space.
Turn your vehicle right to position it directly in front of the alley.
Pull past the alley and stop perpendicular to the outer edge.
Pull past the alley and stop parallel to the outer edge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull past the alley and stop parallel to the outer edge.
questions.explanation: When backing into an alley, first pull past it and stop parallel to the outer edge. Then back your vehicle fully into the alley. Park it straight within the parking space boundaries.

questions.question: When properly adjusted, what should the outside side mirrors on a school bus show the driver?

options.text: The sides of the bus
Under the bus
The front tires touching the ground
Vehicles in front of the bus

questions.correctAnswerText: The sides of the bus
questions.explanation: Properly adjusted outside side mirrors show the driver the sides of the bus, the rear tires touching the ground, and 200 feet behind the bus.

questions.question: During exercises other than straight line backing, you may exit your vehicle to check its position no more than:

options.text: One time.
Two times.
Three times.
Four times.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two times.
questions.explanation: You can exit your vehicle to check its position during the basic control skills test. This is called a "look." During straight line backing, you may do this no more than once. During other exercises, you may do this no more than twice.

questions.question: When checking engine compartment belts during the vehicle inspection test:

options.text: Belts should be checked for tightness with up to three inches of play allowed.
The water pump belt does not need to be identified.
The air compressor belt should be removed.
You must identify any items that are not belt-driven.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must identify any items that are not belt-driven.
questions.explanation: Check the power steering, water pump, alternator, and air compressor belts for cracks and frays. Check for tightness, allowing up to three-quarters of an inch of play at the center of each belt. If any of these items are not belt-driven, identify them and ensure their components work properly, are not damaged or leaking, and are mounted securely.

questions.question: An active railroad crossing:

options.text: Has a traffic control device installed at the crossing.
Does not have any traffic control devices at the crossing.
Has at least 10 vehicles cross the tracks every hour.
Should be avoided.

questions.correctAnswerText: Has a traffic control device installed at the crossing.
questions.explanation: Active railroad crossings have traffic control devices such as flashing red lights, warning bells, and gates. Always follow these devices.

questions.question: Buses may carry:

options.text: Small arms ammunition.
Corrosive materials.
Poison gas.
Explosives other than small arms ammunition.

questions.correctAnswerText: Small arms ammunition.
questions.explanation: Buses can carry small arms ammunition labeled ORM-D, emergency hospital supplies, and drugs. Most other hazardous materials cannot be transported on buses.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, make sure that:

options.text: The emergency exits are hard to open.
The emergency exit warning devices work properly.
The emergency exits squeak.
The emergency exits cannot be opened from inside the cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: The emergency exit warning devices work properly.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, check that emergency exit warning devices work. All emergency exits must open smoothly, be undamaged, and close securely from inside.

questions.question: During the straight line backing exercise, how many times can you exit the vehicle to check its position?

options.text: One time
Two times
Three times
Four times

questions.correctAnswerText: One time
questions.explanation: During the straight line backing exercise, you can exit your vehicle to check its position only one time.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you must be able to do all of the following about oil, except:

options.text: Point to where the dipstick is located.
Show that the oil level is safe for driving.
Show that the oil level is above the refill mark.
Show that the oil level is below the refill mark.

questions.correctAnswerText: Show that the oil level is below the refill mark.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must point to the oil dipstick, show the oil level is safe for driving, and show the oil level is above the refill mark. You should NOT show oil below the refill mark.

questions.question: Outside mirrors on a school bus should be adjusted:

options.text: Before you start the trip.
During the trip.
After students board the bus.
After the trip ends.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start the trip.
questions.explanation: Check and adjust all mirrors on a school bus before starting your trip. Correct mirror adjustment keeps all students and surrounding vehicles safe.

questions.question: If you cannot find a student after they exit the bus, you should:

options.text: Secure the bus and look for the student.
Assume the student exited safely.
Walk to the back of the bus to see if the student got back on.
Ask another student if they have seen the student.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secure the bus and look for the student.
questions.explanation: If you cannot find a student during unloading, secure the bus immediately and check around and under the bus for the missing student.

questions.question: During the on-road driving test, you should:

options.text: Choose your own route to show your driving skills.
Listen to and follow the examiner's directions.
Bring a passenger to ride with you.
Drive in an unsafe manner.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen to and follow the examiner's directions.
questions.explanation: During the on-road driving test, follow the examiner's directions. The examiner will never ask you to drive unsafely.

questions.question: A posted speed limit that is safe for cars:

options.text: Is usually safe for buses to drive at.
May be too fast for a bus.
May be too slow for a bus.
Should be the minimum speed you drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: May be too fast for a bus.
questions.explanation: Posted speed limits, especially on turns and curves, may be safe for cars but too fast for buses. Large vehicle drivers must know how fast their vehicle can safely travel.

questions.question: Before driving a bus that has been parked for a few days, you should:

options.text: Assume the inside is in good condition.
Call the local police department.
Do a walkthrough inspection of the bus.
Ask passengers to check the inside of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do a walkthrough inspection of the bus.
questions.explanation: Unattended buses can be damaged by people. Before driving a bus that has been parked, do a walkthrough inspection inside to make sure it is safe for riders.

questions.question: When inspecting the inside of a bus, you should:

options.text: Loosen every seat.
Check that every handhold is secure.
Assume all buzzers work properly.
Remove the emergency exit handles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that every handhold is secure.
questions.explanation: When inspecting the inside of a bus, make sure everything is safe and works properly. Check that every handhold and railing is firmly in place and safe to use.

questions.question: Before driving a bus that has been left unattended, you should:

options.text: Wash the vehicle thoroughly.
Remove air from the tires.
Check the inside for damage.
Look for any animals that may have gotten on the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the inside for damage.
questions.explanation: Unattended buses can be damaged by people. When checking a bus that has been left unattended, do a walkthrough to check the inside for damage.
